clue.text: Very old article on wood, we hear

indicators.note: the clue asks us to listen, so the words before are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: AN is the indefinite article, placed on top of TEAK, a hardwood

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a very old item seems to be made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue puts the article above the wood; said aloud, the pair sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something dating from long ago, as old furniture or relics are.

clue.text: Panel of people in charge of potato fries?

definitions.text: Panel of people in charge of potato fries?

parts.words: Panel of people in charge of potato fries?
parts.note: a governing body (a board) overseeing chips, the British word for potato fries; really a sheet of compressed wood particles

explanation.surface: A committee is imagined that oversees the making of chips.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, chips are thick potato fries, and a board is a panel of people in charge, so the whimsical reading is a board for chips.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a building panel made from compressed wood chips glued together, used in cheap furniture and flooring.

clue.text: Large source of food for bird

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label meaning large
prey is the animal a hunter feeds on

explanation.surface: A big supply of food is laid out for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating raptor, an example of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Famous race with grand start?

parts.note: the Grand ..., a famous British steeplechase, has the word Grand at its start

explanation.surface: A well-known race begins in impressive style.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous horse race run at Aintree near Liverpool; 'grand start' means its name begins with Grand, not that the race begins grandly.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday short name for the steeplechase, which follows the word Grand in its full title.

clue.text: Police HQ's worst DC, Andy Lane, in trouble

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests these letters are in disarray and must be put back in order

explanation.surface: A detective constable named Andy Lane, the worst at police headquarters, faces disciplinary action.
explanation.walkthrough: DC is a detective constable, which makes the name sound like a real officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, often used as a byname for that force.

clue.text: Well-suited little piece about island traditions?

indicators.note: placed about the other pieces, so the small amount wraps around them

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
lore is a body of traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A small item about an island's customs is described as fitting nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-suited' plays on a suit of clothes as well as on being appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing cut to fit someone exactly, or anything made appropriate for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Winger seen in Scouse line-up

indicators.note: the letters are visible within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A wide player turns up in a Liverpool team selection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a football player, and Scouse means from Liverpool, but here it is a bird, something with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackbird or thrush relative; anything with wings can be called a winger in crosswords.

clue.text: Papa, in bother with Edward, took over

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A father, in trouble alongside Edward, assumed control.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or a child is to take it on as one's own.

clue.text: Creeps from Winchester

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the city name that follows

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant people come from a cathedral city in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeps' looks like a noun for nasty people; it is a verb meaning moves slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To move forward slowly and by small degrees, little by little.

clue.text: Decorative wood was put round stylish bed

indicators.note: the first word is placed around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: in means fashionable
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Ornamental woodwork was fitted around a fashionable bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden panelling on the lower part of a room's walls, often ornamental.

clue.text: Where one might take off songs about drink

indicators.note: the songs are placed about the drink, enclosing it

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Drinking songs are described as where someone might leave in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where aircraft take off, so a passenger's departure point for flight.

clue.text: Young fliers, none with permits

parts.note: O is nought, meaning none
lets means allows

explanation.surface: Young pilots have no licences.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby birds of a nocturnal raptor family, so youngsters that will fly.

clue.text: Aircraft startled your goat

indicators.note: a startled animal scatters, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A low-flying plane frightens a farmer's goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotary-wing flying machine with an unpowered rotor, an early relative of the helicopter.

clue.text: The old and so decrepit climbers might need these

indicators.note: something decrepit is falling to pieces, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Elderly, frail mountaineers might need some support.
explanation.definitionFit: Small ledges or cracks for the feet, which climbers rely on to gain a grip.

clue.text: Frank reveals information on Pikachu, say, when doctor leaves

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal information about them

indicators.note: the doctor leaving means those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: Pikachu is an example of a Pokemon, a creature from the game series
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A frank account exposes secrets about a Pokemon character once its doctor has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is an adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being candid and direct in speech, saying exactly what one thinks.

clue.text: Something smelly and small irritates

parts.note: incense is burned to give off a scent
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A small but smelly thing gets on someone's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone very angry, a stronger form of annoying them.

clue.text: Reportedly stopped woman getting headscarf

indicators.note: this signals the words are judged by how they are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: banned means stopped, and Anna is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman was barred because of her headscarf, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A large patterned cloth tied round the head or neck, a kind of headscarf.

clue.text: Frightened gangster, tooled up?

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster
slang for carrying weapons

explanation.surface: A gangster carrying weapons is described as scared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tooled up' is British slang for carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been given a fright, made anxious by danger, which is the adjectival sense here.

clue.text: Publicity with rhyme that's poor

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a form of publicity
verse is rhyming poetry

explanation.surface: An advert written in verse is judged to be bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfavourable or harmful, as in adverse conditions, a sense close to poor.

clue.text: See drain in need of repair next to the kerb?

indicators.note: something broken has its parts out of place, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken drain is spotted beside the kerb.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, vehicles drive on the left, so the nearside is the left-hand side, next to the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of a vehicle closest to the pavement edge, hence beside the kerb.

clue.text: Claim everything, for example, before end of marriage

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the last one

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: In a divorce, someone claims everything, for example, before the marriage ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is so, typically without proof, a synonym of claim.

clue.text: Gold given to good revolutionary — that's awkward

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Giving gold to a good revolutionary is an embarrassing thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Socially clumsy or lacking grace, a French borrowing for awkward.

clue.text: Girl in one of Noel's songs

definitions.meaning: Noel is Christmas, and its songs are hymns sung in December

explanation.surface: A girl appears in one of the songs of a singer named Noel.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel looks like a singer's name; it is Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name and also a festive hymn sung at Christmas time.

clue.text: Cowardly journalist showing signs of age

parts.note: yellow means lacking courage
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A timid reporter is starting to look old.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper and fabric turn a pale brownish colour as they age, so this shows age.

clue.text: Maria, so upset about second-class and first-class fare

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the next piece, enclosing it
upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-class

explanation.surface: Maria is distressed by second-class and first-class meals on her trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-class' looks like a second wordplay grade, but 'first-class fare' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the food of the gods, so the finest possible food.

clue.text: A film of lubricant?

definitions.meaning: the 1978 musical starring John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John
an oily substance used to reduce friction

explanation.surface: A thin coating of lubricating oil is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A film of' reads as a thin layer; the clue splits into a movie and a lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous musical movie title and a thick oily substance applied to machinery.

clue.text: Worshipped graven image: i.e. I'd sold out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to selling a revered carved image they worshipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graven image' is part of the definition: to worship one is to make it an idol.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated as an idol, a graven image being an object of worship.
